newsitem.title: Poland: Russian parliament official says NATO archaic.
newsitem.headline: Russian parliament official says NATO archaic.

text.p: The chairman of Russia's parliament, Gennady Seleznov, reiterating Moscow's opposition to eastward expansion of NATO, on Sunday dismissed the Western alliance as an "archaicism", the Polish news agency PAP reported.
"When the Warsaw Pact disintegrated, people held the view that this finally marked the end of military systems," Seleznyov told a news conference in Poland.
"Now we see plans to enlarge NATO, whilst in our society there exists the conviction that NATO is an archaicism in the 21st century."
Poland is one of three former Soviet allies in Eastern Europe widely forecast to be admitted to NATO later this year.

Commenting on an emerging anti-NATO group in the Duma (lower house), Seleznyov said that while the Russian executive and legislature disagreed on some matters, they were united in opposing NATO's eastward expansion, PAP said.
"We have one thing in common (with the anti-NATO group) -- we do not consider the Pact's expansion up to our borders necessary," he said.
"While we have no moral or political right to forbid other countries to implement their goals and ensure their security, we do have the right to explain our fears."
Seleznyov, speaking in the southern Polish city of Krakow, said the Kremlin remained in favour of full nuclear disarmament.
